core_obligations: Define W as the union of the images of the morphisms g of the prescribed type whose base change has P, and note that each such g is open, so W is open (proof lines 5596-5606).
Show that X_W -> W has P by applying tau locality to the covering formed by the g's (proof lines 5606-5610).
Prove assertion (1): any such base change has image inside W by construction (proof line 5610).
Prove assertion (2): the inclusion one way from base-change stability, the other from the definition of W (proof lines 5610-5618).
Deduce assertion (3) from (2) using the shape of a tau-covering (proof lines 5618-5620).
proof_roadmap: Construction of W and openness (proof lines 5596-5606).
Locality gives the property on W, i.e. existence and (1) (proof lines 5606-5610).
difficulty_reason: For a property P of morphisms that is tau local on the target for tau in {fppf, syntomic, smooth, etale}, the lemma constructs the largest open W(f) of the base Y on which the restriction of f has P, and proves three compatibilities: a base change along a flat locally finitely presented, syntomic, smooth or etale morphism landing in P has image inside W(f) (1), W commutes with such base change (2), and W is compatible with tau-coverings (3) (statement lines 5576-5593). The proof is a genuine construction: W is defined as the union of the images of all such morphisms g whose base change has P; these g are open, so W is open; locality of P in the tau topology then shows X_W -> W has P because the g's form a covering of W, which gives existence and (1); the reverse inclusion for (2) is obtained by observing that an open Y'' of Y' over which P holds must factor through W by construction; and (3) is a consequence of (2) since the maps of a tau-covering have the required shape (proof lines 5595-5620). The level is H3: the object is built rather than quoted, and each of the three compatibility statements is derived from the construction.
